summary: Interpreted the cadence experiment (CheckRun a4a0cbfa094b4d1982032d9de0652861, exit 0, tests_passed) and used it to narrow my own earlier claim. Parsed index 0 is the emptied state (store_last=0, snapshot_index=3, applied_index=3, one stored snapshot, should_snapshot=true); parsed indices 1-2 show the node's own snapshot loop adding snapshots at the unchanged index 3 while the applied index stayed 3 (count 1→2 by 203ms, →3 by 405ms); parsed indices 3-6 then show the count flat at 3 through 1209ms with should_snapshot still true. So the redundant snapshot work happens and is repeatable, but it is not one snapshot per interval, and this run does not establish why the count plateaued (attempts not stored, or attempts no longer made - the harness recorded neither). I therefore withdraw the earlier 'schedules a snapshot at the unchanged index on each interval' phrasing; the evidenced claim is the persistent spurious verdict while the store index stays below the snapshot index, causing redundant snapshots at an unchanged index, observed twice. The defect assertion itself stands on that persistent spurious verdict plus the observed redundant work, with limitations recording the unknown recurrence rate, the store-specific wrapped store_last, the non-production 100ms interval, and the single in-process execution.
